subject: Post-call recap: spend capacity, batching & next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Markus Wagner <markus@ledgerly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:10:00 -0400
Subject: Quick recap + budget-first next steps (token economics & batching)

Hi Samantha / Markus — thanks again for the time today. Short call recap focused on the spend constraints you shared and the practical levers we can test quickly. Please read and confirm anything I missed.

Pain points you shared
- Monthly inference spend currently unpredictable; finance asked for a hard cap ($/month) and a proposal that shows concrete levers to get under it.
- Peak latency for user-facing flows must stay under ~220ms P95.
- High percentage of short prompts (avg token length ~45) but lots of repeated prefixes (session system prompts + product metadata).
- Security: need SOC2 evidence and audit logs for any pilot.

Goals we heard
- Keep initial pilot spend <= $20k/month (preferred by Finance); breakout scenarios if they can go to $30k/mo.
- Validate 30–50% effective cost reduction using batching + KV-prefix caching within a 4–6 week pilot.
- Confirm quality preserved (accept minor latency tradeoffs if overall cost fits).

Estimated quick-economic sketch (back-of-envelope from today)
- Current baseline: ~12M tokens/day across key flows (~360M tokens/month).
- Target unit cost to hit $20k/mo: ~0.055$/k token (we should refine).
- Expected levers: batching (estimated 20–35% savings on token ops for your request profile), prefix/KV caching (another 10–25% effective savings for repeated system prompts), model quantization (8-bit variant possible for non-critical paths ~10–15% savings).

Proposed next steps (pick one)
1) 3-week cashflow-aware pilot (hosted + caching, focused on high-volume routes) — Redwood provides TCO model and implementation checklist.
2) Hybrid pilot (hosted baseline + reserved burst or Dedicated for steady throughput) — requires short sizing call with infra ops.

Requested from you
- Confirm whether Finance will accept a $20k/mo guardrail or prefer $30k as the upper bound.
- Share a 48-hour sample of token counts by route (anonymized) and an internal stakeholder for procurement (Jordan in call?).

Attachments: redwood-tco-onepager.pdf (one-page cost levers), ledgerly-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP template)

I can turn today’s sketch into a short TCO spreadsheet and a pilot MAP by EOD. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with Markus & Jordan this week.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@ledgerly.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Wagner <markus@ledgerly.com>, Jordan Price <jordan@ledgerly.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick recap + budget-first next steps (token economics & batching)

Thanks Sean — helpful summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget guardrail: Finance is comfortable with an initial commitment of up to $18k/mo for a 4–6 week pilot. If we see >25% net savings in-week 3 we can consider stretching to $25–30k for the production rollout.
2) Token sample: I'll upload a 48-hour anonymized sample to the Drive link you shared by EOD today.
3) Compliance: SOC2 attestation and request logs are required; can you send the SOC2 cover page and details on retention windows?
4) Stakeholders: Jordan (CFO) and Markus (CTO) should be on the follow-up — Jordan prefers mornings (9–11am ET) this week.

Also, Markus asked whether Redwood can guarantee a fallback to a lower-cost model variant automatically if the budget guardrail is breached.

I'll schedule a 30-min slot for Wed 05/05 09:30am ET if that works for you and Marissa.

—Samantha
Head of Product Operations | Ledgerly
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick recap + budget-first next steps (token economics & batching)

Sean — quick internal note based on Sam's $18k cap: 
- Recommend proposing a hybrid pilot: hosted baseline with automatic prefix caching + a reserved burst pool (small Dedicated slice) that kicks in for sustained throughput. This gives predictable unit pricing for the heavy tail while keeping operational lift low.
- For the proposal we'll run two scenarios in the TCO sheet: (A) conservative: $18k cap — > expected savings 22–28% (B) stretch: $25k cap — > expected savings 35–48% with small Dedicated slice + aggressive caching and batching.
- I'll run a run-rate simulation using their 48h sample once Sam uploads; can deliver updated numbers tonight.

Also: confirm that SOC2 cover page + audit contact will be sent by security@redwood.com.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@ledgerly.com>, Markus Wagner <markus@ledgerly.com>, Jordan Price <jordan@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick recap + budget-first next steps (token economics & batching)

Appreciate the quick replies — confirming next steps and timeline below.

What Redwood will deliver by EOD today
- Updated TCO worksheet with two scenarios (18k cap / 25k stretch) + clear per-1M-token unit costs and projected monthly spend.
- SOC2 cover page and retention policy summary (sent from security@redwood.com).
- MAP draft (ledgerly-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with roles, milestone dates, and acceptance criteria.

Proposed pilot plan (start: week of 05/10)
- Week 0 (prep): onboarding + Dev API keys, sample log ingestion, MAP sign-off.
- Week 1–3 (pilot): enable batching + prefix caching on top routes, run hosted baseline; monitor cost delta daily.
- Week 4 (evaluation): review economics, ops, and quality; if >25% net savings we switch to the hybrid reserved burst approach.

Immediate asks from Ledgerly
- Confirm Wed 05/05 09:30am ET for 30-min follow-up (Jordan + Markus + Samantha).
- Upload the 48-hour token sample to the Drive link.
- Quick confirmation that $18k is the acceptable hard cap for the pilot.

If those three are green I’ll include a lightweight SOW paragraph in the MAP and an initial invoice template for procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-tco-onepager.pdf, ledgerly-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
